newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-RELAXED ENGLAND HEAD FOR TOURNOI DE FRANCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RELAXED ENGLAND HEAD FOR TOURNOI DE FRANCE.

text.p: The message was professionally done, charming, polite and reassuring.
"Ladies and Gentlemen, I'd like to ask you to fasten your safety belts, sit back in your seats and relax. The flying time to London is two hours. I hope you all have a pleasant flight."

Paul Gascoigne's unmistakable Geordie lilt raised a smile over the intercom of the midnight charter carrying home the England party -- and around 200 assorted media, sponsors and other officials -- after another far more important professional job had been achieved.

England's 2-0 victory over Poland in Chorzow was accomplished with all the efficiency, discipline and hard work normally associated with Germany. On a freezing night in Chorzow, England played some of their best football since the heady hot days of last summer's Euro '96.
It was a performance that took England close to qualifying for next year's World Cup Finals in France and means that their next trip to France should be a relaxed one.
They return to the continent on Monday for the four-nation Tournoi de France and matches against Italy on Wednesday, France on Saturday and Brazil on Tuesday week.

Glenn Hoddle, praised by the media on Sunday for his team's performance in Chorzow, will use those three games to experiment with his side as he prepares for England's final push towards France '98 in the autumn.
"The fact we'll be playing Italy next week and then again in a vital World Cup qualifier in October makes no difference to the outcome of the game in Rome," he said.
"I'll use the matches to put some thoughts into practice and hopefully the whole week in France will be great preparation for the World Cup next year which I am sure we will qualify for."

England's win eliminated the Poles from the World Cup and means that England can still qualify automatically for France '98 if they win their home match against Moldova and their away game in Rome -- irrespective of whether Italy beat Georgia in September.
At the worst England have guaranteed second spot in the group and a place in the playoffs, but their record is currently the best of all nine second-placed European teams.
If they finish the qualifiers still with the best record, they will qualify automatically. The other eight qualifers will meet in two-legged play-offs.

Alan Shearer, who scored the opening goal against Poland, said: "We are all looking forward to France now and I am sure it would have been much harder if we had lost in Poland. I don't think you'll be able to read too much into the team that plays in France -- but this is the way forward for any international side."
Shearer's fifth minute strike and a second goal in the last minute from Teddy Sheringham secured England's first competitive win in Poland.
And Gascoigne proved England had plenty to smile about with his cheery message -- even though a gashed thigh forced him off after only 17 minutes and out of England's game against Italy on Wednesday.
But England will do well not to be too over-confident as there is a historical precedent for the situation against Italy which many English fans remember only too well.
In 1976 England came from two goals down to beat Italy 3-2 in the American Bicentennial Tournament at Yankee Stadium, a few months before playing in Italy in a World Cup qualifier.
They went to Rome full of confidence, got beaten 2-0 and missed out on the 1978 World Cup finals in Argentina. A win over Italy on Wednesday will be greeted with muted confidence at best.
